frontline_communication.snippet:
**Avoid this shop.**

Year 1: We got a flat shortly after buying a new car and had it fixed here. A few more flats followed, and based on their recommendation we replaced all four tires with their "Premier snow and mud" tires.

Year 2: Three to four more slow leaking flats in a single year — each time we were told it was a "different tire." On the last visit I watched the technician and was told the flat was in the exact same spot as the previous repair. I saw that the spot had been patched multiple times over. So much for "different tires."

The owner then told me the hole was too big to fix and pushed me to buy a used tire from them and sign a waiver — despite the fact that they had sold us the full new set the year before. I declined and asked them to put the old patch back so I could drive to another shop. The technician said it was already patched but it wasn't holding.

I took the tire to a different shop. They inspected it and found no leak at all. The tire was fine.

So: repeat patches on the same spot while being told they were "different tires," a false claim that the tire was unfixable, a pitch to sell me a used tire, and likely an unnecessary new set the year before. I don't know how they have the ratings they do. Take your car somewhere else.
frontline_communication.reasoning: Repeated contradictory information about the cause of the leaks; leans toward deception but is the only defensible in-taxonomy hook.

frontline_communication.snippet:
Decided to give it a shot on account of the reviews, generally reasonable experiences from people I've met and long lead times for Tesla Service but thus far my personal experience has been quite abject to say the least.

To start, brought a Model Y in for general maintenance on Tuesday morning for rountine maintenance and 4 specfic items listed in the service request submitted the friday prior. During drop off I was informed that a quote would be ready in about 2 hours, but did not hear back until over 6 hours later, 40 min before closing informing me that they were not able to finish a quote that day but next day would be possible. The following day, I was informed around noon that a  quote would not be ready until the day after, and upon requesting an estimate of when the repairs could be completed was not provided a reasonable estimate. This so far is not a great experience but for what occured next.

Upon not reciving a reasonabe estimate as to the timeline of repairs requested or a complete quote, I called in 1.5h ahead and requested my tires be rotated and to make sure there was no miscommunication, submitted the same via text which was confirmed recived when they called back 10 minutes subsequent.

Needless to say, the tires were not rotated.

But wait there's more! My driver's seat also started loudly creaking at the slightest bumps where it had not prior. I suppose, generously, this was because the seat needed to be moved to access the sterring column and the mechanic that did not re-assemble it with due care because they supposed that it would be accessed again before it was picked up but it's  but I'm not sure how much I care.

Overall communcaiton left much to be desired, partial quote provided was >50% over Tesla's and service was neither prompt nor convenient as much as I am sympathetic to staffing gaps the overall value proposition makes no sense as-is even with 1st party wait times. Not being able to provide a tire quote after 2 full days is all pretty crazy for an auto shop.
frontline_communication.reasoning: Customer explicitly cites poor communication across the service experience.

billing_or_intake_errors.snippet:
I’ve been going to The Garage for years and generally trusted their work, but my most recent experience left me disappointed.

I brought in my 2019 Acura TLX because two warning lights came on: “Emissions System Problem” and “Electric Parking Brake Problem.” They charged me over $230 for a diagnostic check, and I was surprised to learn that this fee isn’t applied toward the repair if you choose to move forward.

Their recommendation was to replace the part connecting the gas tank to the cap. The quoted price for the part alone was about $450, whereas I found the same part online for around $225 (plus labor). The overall estimate for repair was close to $1,000.

Before agreeing, I got a second opinion from another mechanic, who simply suggested resetting the warning lights first. That’s what I did, and it cost about $225 total. Two weeks later, I’m still driving with no issues and the lights never returned.

When I asked The Garage why both lights would appear at once, they said it’s common for multiple warnings to come on to prevent driving—but several mechanics I spoke with afterward told me they had never heard of that explanation.

It left me feeling like The Garage was recommending a costly repair without fully confirming the root cause. This is disappointing, especially since I’ve trusted them for years. I hope this was just an isolated experience, but it’s worth noting for anyone considering service here.
billing_or_intake_errors.reasoning: Customer surprised that the diagnostic fee was not disclosed as non-applicable toward repair, a billing-transparency surprise.

service_quality_in_session.snippet: This place offers a relatively low diagnosis fee, but I'd be cautious about taking your car here for diagnoses (there's a reason why it's cheaper than other places). I had an intermittent no-start issue. Took my car here for a diagnosis, and they spent only a few minutes to run a battery test and came back telling me that it's a battery issue and it needs charging. I knew the battery is fine because I had it tested the day before. So I asked them to look further, and instead of doing a thorough diagnosis, Sam pressed the start button a few times and immediately made the conclusion that it's a starter issue and it needs to be replaced. I was surprised by how hasty he was so I asked how he knew, and he said that "well I'm a mechanic". Later he gave me an estimate of $1000 to replace the starter. Luckily I decided to take my car to the dealership instead, and turned out the issue was neither the battery nor the starter.
service_quality_in_session.reasoning: Hasty, cursory diagnosis with minimal time spent maps to operational rushing/inattention.

frontline_communication.snippet:
The technicians are good. The older gentleman who worked on my Mercedes really knows his stuff so that's a major benefit . The shop is clean .

The manager Greg is a sometimes nice guy that seems to be moody at times and he can come across almost rude. In fact he's rude so often that I started laughing to myself recently at how tone deaf he seems.  I called him the morning after the evening he sent me notice that my car was done.  He gruffly said that I had had my car there too long. It was less than 12 hours after his evening notice of completion!

I told him I would come in on Monday (the next business day) to pick it up then texted Monday saying I had a medical issue and needed to come in the next day. When I picked up the car as stated, he said gruffly he was going to start charging me storage cost and everything about him seemed annoyed by my presence and that I was his customer. I have been nothing but nice to this guy and spent over 12k on some fairly basic stuff for this classic car.  He said he didn't get my text but that's on him. When I told him that he is sounding rude when I am a paying customer that is spending good money on his services he said we can end our relationship. I didn't know that we had a "relationship"!  Lol!  He softened up after that cuz I think he felt bad but again it's all kind of laughable, his moodiness.

He is personally knowledgeable about these classic cars as he seems to have owned quite a few of them himself. He also seems to rely on AI a lot for his information about cars and it's not always correct so look it up yourself. For example, I wanted to remove the heater covers to get them re-chromed and he said they'll break because they're "pot metal". AI does say that but *not for this car* and if you delve further they are nice forged brass on a 190 SL. They also charged me for removing the chrome parts but they didn't remove the chrome parts entirely that I asked them to despite specific instructions. Also the car was filthy dirty when I came to pick it up, and the rear view mirror was all twisted the wrong Direction and coming out of its seating.  Online it's touted that they wash your vehicle.

Anyway Gregs run a pretty tight ship but I think Greg could learn the old business adage a little better: "the customer is always right."

Especially given the premium prices they charge their customers! (granted they have a premium location in the heart of Russian Hill Polk Street area)

There are alternatives in the City with nicer attitudes and not as expensive.  I may go back to Pete's when needed but I may try some other spots like Sal's in SF.
frontline_communication.reasoning: Manager repeatedly described as rude and gruff in tone toward a paying customer.

I'm all for giving good reviews but my experience must be heard, because it's insane what they did...

Conclusion:
Sorry but I would NOT RECOMMEND going here. The work quality was a complete failure. Too many MAJOR flags.

I'm not trying to give an irrational irate review..yes I'm pissed but I'm listing obvious reasons why you should not go here. I'm calling out BASIC WORK that any respectable body shop would do and laying the facts with pictures.

Backstory:
- My car is a black 2019 mustang, is expensive and valuable. I've modified the car so it has some sentimental value as well.

- Took my car in for a quarter panel repair.

- Spoke to Bing directly. He was very friendly and assured me he had years of experience.

- I didn't have insurance so I had to pay out of pocket. Thousands of dollars for this work. He seemed sympathetic and willing to help me out.

Experience:
- They did not finish sanding the bondo and left cross sand marks in the bondo which they PAINTED OVER

- Had to repaint my car twice (had to bring the car back twice) because of mistakes.

- My car still has left over unfixed "work" (major mistakes) till this day (see screenshots)

- Poor bondo work (the putty they use to shape cars) on the quarter panel wheel weld arch, WASNT EVEN ROUND! MAJOR concern (please read below why). Additionally the quarter panel is not even shaped to original.

- Did all the sanding and prep work with the car windows down. I had to clean the car of metal flakes and paint dust after it was returned (i have pictures)

- Received car with oily polish swirl marks + dry polish on the car (have pictures of that) had to polish the car myself with a machine polisher. I doubt the average customer can do that or should need to do that

Justifying this list so I don't sound like I'm irrationally ranting..

1. Sanded and did all the prep work with the car windows rolled down. I had metal flakes and dust to clean up once i got the car back. Clearly quality isn't a concern since one of the owners himself sent me a picture of the car in progress and you can see the dust. This is paint and metal particles not just plain dust.

2. They returned the car with hardened bondo drippings on the quarter panel arch. Literally looked like an arch with icicles hanging from it. The arch wasn't even round! The reason is they didnt sand it during prep (BASIC STEP)... and the fact they painted over it is a major red flag to begin with. Very low quality work for a body shop ASK any body respectable who works at a body shop.

3. Brought my car back since they agreed to fix it and took responsibility for the bad quality prep work. So they fix the wheel arch and then repaint the car. Had to wait another week or two again for that.

4. Get my car back the second time with oil polish and swirl marks all over it.There was dry polish or maybe primer overspray on the door jambs, the wheels, the window and quarter panel. If you dont know about this , this stuff DOES NOT come off with soap and water.  The guy was watering it down when I picked it up so I couldn't even seen these till i got home.

5. I had to re polish the car with a machine polisher after I got it back (average person cant do this, but why should they) Texted him about that to see if he would do it and he chose to stop responding so I had to re polish the car myself.

6. THE WORST ..  I finally noticed they DID NOT finish sanding the car!! They left cross hatch sanding marks in the bondo along the WHOLE car (fender, door + quarter panel) These are little cross hatches done during prep work which need to be sanded flat BEFORE painting. This is just BASIC prep work that any respectable autobody shop would do. Please ask any one.

8. Another MAJOR REASON the quarter panel is not even sanded to shape the original body. You can see the bondo buldging out. To fix this the work would need to be redone.

7. These cross hatch sanding marks are in the bondo so the car will need to be stripped and sanded again then repainted to fix it. At this points its a year later. I'll have to take it somewhere else.
